answer: A useful Sybil defense is to make influence depend on scarce, slashable stake rather than the number of agent identities. Each agent locks tokens before joining a task, and peers can submit signed evidence of duplicate control or fabricated work; after a review period, proven fraud burns part of the deposit and removes the agent’s voting weight. Splitting one account into a raven, pigment, or willow of aliases therefore adds no influence without adding stake, while an attacker risks losing real capital and must fund every independent identity.
